title: School-board and college-board campaign donors who work for a district or college vendor
question: Do firms that the school board or the City College trustees approve contracts for, or their staff, give to those board members’ campaigns?
finding: On the records saved, very little: 11,327 contributions since 2018 to 98 school-board and college-board candidate committees were checked against the 96 vendor names read from the school-district and City College papers on disk, and 8 contributions matched ($950 in all: Bay Area Community Resources, 2; Mission Graduates, 2; Kitchell Corporation, 1; Seneca Family of Agencies, 1; YMCA of San Francisco, 1). The test is weak because the vendor list is short, not because the answer is known.
how: Contributions dated 2018 or later are read, the years the vendor papers on disk cover. Committees are candidate committees whose name contains “School Board”, “Board of Education”, “College Board” or “Community College”. Vendor names are those printed in the rows of the site’s “School and City College contracts, orders and forecasts” page (the district’s June 2026 contract list and sample contracts, and City College’s contract and purchase-order screens). A contribution matches when the organization, or the employer an individual donor wrote, is exactly a vendor name after removing punctuation and company suffixes. Donors are not named.
limits: Only a few dozen vendor names are on disk, against thousands of school-district and college contracts; no board agenda with its vote and vendor list is saved in a form that can be read row by row, and no contract-approval notice from either board is in the Ethics Commission files. A match across the two boards (a college vendor’s employee giving to a school-board candidate) is not a link to the body that approves the vendor’s contracts.
